articles.headline: Lions linebacker Jack Campbell placed on backboard, carted off vs. Vikings
articles.description: Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell was placed on a backboard and carted off the field early in the fourth quarter Sunday against the Vikings.
articles.headlineJa: ライオンズのラインバッカー、ジャック・キャンベルがバックボードで搬送、バイキングス戦で退場
articles.descriptionJa: ライオンズのオールプロ・ラインバッカー、ジャック・キャンベルが日曜日のバイキングス戦、第4クォーター序盤にバックボードに固定され、カートでフィールド外へ運ばれた。
articles.body:
DETROIT -- Lions All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell was placed on a backboard and carted off the field early in the fourth quarter Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings.

He is being taken to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury, according to the Lions.

Campbell was face down on the turf and was not moving after hitting tight end T.J. Hockenson for his third tackle of the game. He was evaluated by medical personnel before being strapped to a board and carefully lifted onto a cart to a round of applause.

Detroit's entire team and most of the coaching staff surrounded the cart before it transported Campbell off the field for further evaluation.

The former Iowa star was drafted by the Lions with the No. 18 pick in 2023. Last season, Campbell was an All-Pro selection after becoming the first NFL player in seven years to have 150-plus tackles and at least five sacks and three forced fumbles.

The Lions signed Campbell last May to a four-year contract extension that runs through the 2030 season.

He was one of three key Lions defenders injured in the game, along with pass rusher DJ Wonnum and safety Brian Branch, who suffered concussions earlier in the game.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Inside the complicated injury history of Ravens' Lamar Jackson
articles.description: If the QB's health record has taught the football world anything, his timeline to return can be challenging.
articles.headlineJa: レイブンズ、ラマー・ジャクソンの複雑な怪我の履歴に迫る
articles.descriptionJa: このQBの健康記録がフットボール界に教えてくれたことがあるとすれば、それは彼の復帰までの道のりが困難な場合があるということだ。
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson's 2026 season is turning into the most injury-filled one of his nine-year career.

Jackson missed three games with a high left ankle sprain and returned only to injure his right thumb on his first snap of Sunday's game at the Buffalo Bills.

If Jackson's injury history has taught the football world anything, his timeline to return can be complicated and an extended absence can derail the Ravens' season. But ultimately, the only one who truly knows when Jackson will return is Jackson himself.

"Look, if he's able to play, [is] healthy enough to play and play the way that obviously we feel like he needs to play, then he will play," coach Jesse Minter said Monday.

Two weeks ago, there was a feeling within the team that Jackson was going to be able to play last Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals. He practiced as a limited participant all week, worked with the first-team offense that Friday and took part in the television production meetings, which usually signifies he will be the starting quarterback.

But Jackson was ruled out last Saturday after he experienced increased swelling in his injured left ankle, according to a report during the CBS game broadcast. Tracy Wolfson, the sideline reporter for Sunday's game, posted on social media that it "came as a shock to the Ravens that Lamar couldn't go." Minter later said that was "a little bit" of a mischaracterization.

In his first comments since getting injured two weeks ago, Jackson made it clear last week that the decision to play comes down to pain tolerance. It still hurts for Jackson to plant his foot when running.

"If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play," Jackson said. "But [if] I'm restricted and I can't  do what I do, [then] I'm not helping [anybody]. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that's not helping my team at all."

Jackson has now missed multiple games because of injury in four of his past six seasons, but it's a flawed narrative to describe him as the NFL's most injured quarterback. Jackson, who has been sidelined for 17 games with injuries (excluding COVID and illness), has missed fewer games than four other starting quarterbacks -- Kyler Murray (31), Dak Prescott (26), Daniel Jones (25) and Joe Burrow (22) -- since 2019.

"It seems like Lamar's the only quarterback that kind of gets the slander that he gets for anytime anything is going on," Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey said earlier this month. "I feel like you just don't see these same articles, and you don't see these same headlines. I think it's unfair treatment."

Humphrey added, "I just feel like it goes -- sometimes it seems like it gets away from -- I don't know if it's because of lack of agent or what, that no one can kind of defend him. I do know this: If Lamar Jackson can play, if he's healthy enough to play, he will play."

When Jackson misses time, it can turn the Ravens from a championship contender to a team struggling to make the postseason

articles.headline: Arteta says Arsenal 'loved the mission' in first Anfield win since 2012
articles.description: Mikel Arteta said his players "loved the mission" of winning at Liverpool for the first time in 14 years as he hailed Sunday's "historic" 1-0 victory at Anfield.
articles.headlineJa: アルテタ監督、2012年以来初のアニフィールド勝利に「ミッションを楽しんでいた」と語る
articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・アルテタ監督は、日曜日のアニフィールドでの「歴史的」な1-0の勝利を称賛し、選手たちが14年ぶりとなるリヴァプールでの勝利という「ミッションを楽しんでいた」と語った。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta said his players "loved the mission" of winning at Liverpool for the first time in 14 years as he hailed Sunday's "historic" 1-0 victory at Anfield.

Kai Havertz's 16th-minute strike was enough to secure a narrow win in a hard-fought game that sent the Gunners three points clear at the top of the Premier League ahead of Manchester City.

Liverpool put Arsenal under huge pressure after falling behind, but the visitors kept them at bay with a more controlled second-half display, and the Reds ended without registering a shot on target for the first time ever in a Premier League home game.

Arsenal had lost eight of their past 13 league games and kept just one clean sheet in 27 previous league visits to Anfield before Sunday.

"[They are] just loving the mission," said Arteta. "And the mission was something that we didn't accomplish in 14 years. There were reasons for that. Some of them were psychological problems. Some of them were related to the quality that we showed on the pitch, certain moments or decisions.

"And we knew that we need to nail absolutely all of them. And we're going to have to navigate through periods that we're going to have to suffer because they are extremely good at doing that and creating those vertical attacks, those chaos moments for almost nothing.

"You really need to enjoy that. If you don't, there will be a moment they will switch up and they will punish you. And yeah, I think the way we competed and played and the chances that we generated as well, it was really impressive. So I'm really happy."

Arsenal, after being dumped out of the Carabao Cup by League Two side Fleetwood Town in midweek, responded with a defiant display to extend their record in the Premier League to eight wins and one loss from nine games.

"We're extremely proud of what the team, the players, everybody's done especially in the conditions that we arrived to this game, where we were after the defeat against Liverpool, it looks like the end of the world," Arteta said. "It looks like, 'Yeah, what are we doing?' And then you have to pick yourself up and understand that this is a beautiful part of this game.

"It can take you to really bad places, but four days later you have the opportunity to do something really historic, and we've done it."

articles.headline: Buccaneers beat Falcons 16-0 despite failing to complete a single pass in wet, sloppy conditions
articles.description: — Baker Mayfield didn’t complete a pass but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0 on Sunday behind Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell's rushing on a wet, sloppy field.
articles.headlineJa: バッカニアーズ、悪天候でパス成功ゼロながらファルコンズに16-0で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: ベイカー・メイフィールドはパスを一本も成功させなかったが、日曜日の雨でぬかるんだフィールドにおいて、バッキー・アービングとケニー・ゲインウェルのラン攻撃を武器に、タンパベイ・バッカニアーズがアトランタ・ファルコンズに16-0で勝利した。
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- — Baker Mayfield didn’t complete a pass but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0 on Sunday behind Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell's rushing on a wet, sloppy field.


              The Buccaneers (3-5) set a team record for yards rushing in a game with 324, and became the first team to have zero completions since Buffalo on Sept. 29, 1974. The Bills beat the Jets 16-12 in that one, and that had been the only time a team didn’t complete a pass in the Super Bowl era.


              Irving ran for 170 yards and one touchdown on 27 carries, Gainwell ran for 140 on 25 carries and Chase McLaughlin kicked three field goals to stay perfect this season at 19 for 19.


              Playing in a driving rain for most of the afternoon, Mayfield was 0 for 3 in his second game back after missing three weeks with a fractured thumb.


              Michael Penix Jr. went 8 for 24 for 125 yards with four interceptions for Atlanta (3-5). Bijan Robinson was held to 76 yards on 19 carries.


              Facing his former coach with Cleveland, Mayfield didn’t have to do much with his arm. He scrambled for 13 yards while Irving and Gainwell piled up big numbers. Mayfield and Kevin Stefanski are the only QB-coach combination to win a playoff game for the Browns in the 2000s but they didn’t have a close relationship. Mayfield was upset that Stefanski didn’t reach out to him after the Browns traded him to Carolina in 2022.


              Tampa Bay’s previous rushing high was 283 yards — including 235 from Doug Martin — in a 45-17 win at Philadelphia on Nov. 22, 2015.


              Irving’s 4-yard TD run in the third quarter gave the Buccaneers a 16-0 lead and the offense kept pounding the ball on the ground.


              Nick Folk missed a 53-yard field goal wide left on Atlanta’s opening series and McLaughlin made one from 46 yards out on the next series.


              The Bucs missed an opportunity after Alex Anzalone picked off Penix at Atlanta’s 41 and returned it 8 yards, and an unsportsmanlike penalty on Drake London put the ball at the 18. But Irving fumbled out of the end zone for a touchback after taking a lateral from Mayfield. Jessie Bates III forced the fumble.


              Anzalone picked off Penix again on Atlanta’s next possession to set up Tampa Bay at the Falcons 19. But the Buccaneers couldn’t go anywhere and settled for McLaughlin’s 34-yarder that made it 6-0.


              After Jacob Parrish picked off Penix on a fourth-down pass at Tampa Bay’s 17, the Buccaneers drove 65 yards and McLaughlin connected from 42 yards to extend the lead to 9-0.


              Last week, Tampa Bay beat the Panthers 43-13 with Mayfield completing just 7 of 11 passes for 64 yards.


              The Bucs have won three of four since an 0-4 start and are just a half-game behind Carolina (3-4) in the NFC South.

articles.headline: NFL Week 8's best arrivals, led by Rams' Quentin Lake
articles.description: Here's a look at the best-dressed players around the NFL in Week 8.
articles.body:
On the afternoon following Halloween, Los Angeles Rams defensive back Quentin Lake decided to rock a fit adopting a look simulating Neo from the Matrix.

 

Lake's all-black look is one of the best fits of the season regardless of the costume theme. But the question is: does Lake prefer to take the red pill or the blue pill?

The long-flowing trench coat is the star of this fit, but I love the commitment to the bit with black-tinted sunglasses and black combat boots supporting the look.

It's always a perfect reminder of fall hitting warm-weather states like California allowing players to be more versatile with their looks.

Secondary shoutout to Lake's teammate -- Rams receiver Puka Nacua -- who also went with a trench coat vibe, except his is layered with an inner black leather jacket with overlapping lapel from luxury brand Umit Benan.

The Rams trench coat duo sets the standard for Week 8's best gameday tunnel fits. Here are more top Week 8 fits that caught our eye:

Along with the Rams showing their versatility this week, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce came dripped out in the earth tones and a leather jacket.

Sunday's best

Minnesota Vikings' quarterback Kyler Murray and wide receiver Justin Jefferson reported to their duties in similar monochromatic looks, with Murray styling a double-breasted look with a white tank and a beanie to match.

Thursday night fashion

Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young opted for a clean Louis Vuitton shirt with a heavy jacket on top and sleek sunglasses. On the other side, Green Bay Packers safety Javon Bullard went with a denim tie shirt from the clothing brand Jagne.

articles.headline: Arsenal hold on for a big win at Liverpool, one Iraola & Co. can learn from
articles.description: Arsenal's defense held firm against the Reds' expensive attack to notch a famous win at Anfield for the first time since 2012. However, there were positive signs for Liverpool when it came to their intensity and effort.
articles.body:
LIVERPOOL -- Arsenal made a huge statement in the Premier League title race by securing a 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

 
A first-half goal from Kai Havertz was enough to seal the Gunners' first win at Liverpool's home stadium in over 14 years. The result sees Mikel Arteta's move to the top of the Premier League table, three points clear of second-placed Manchester City.

 
Havertz opened the scoring inside 17 minutes, tapping in at the far post from Declan Rice's cross. However, Liverpool responded well to the early setback and were frustrated not to have been awarded a penalty for Jurriën Timber's shirt pull on Alexander Isak inside the box.

 
The Reds came close to restoring parity late in the first half when Alexis Mac Allister nodded over the bar after a dangerous ball into the box from Milos Kerkez. Arsenal later had a big chance to double their lead when Christos Tzolis saw his low drive tipped around the post by Alisson. Ultimately though, Havertz's goal was enough to secure all three points for Arteta's side and to end Liverpool's five-game winning run in all competitions. -- Beth Lindop

1. Arsenal end their Anfield hoodoo with gritty defensive display

Arsenal just don't win at Anfield. They have not recorded a victory on this ground since Sept. 2012 -- when manager Mikel Arteta was a player. Often they have crumbled here -- think 4-0 in 2021, 5-1 in 2018 or 4-0 in 2017 -- and even last season when there were already early signs that Liverpool looked vulnerable in their title defence, Arsenal were too passive and lost to a brilliant 83rd-minute Dominik Szoboszlai free-kick.

- VAR Review: Were Liverpool denied a clear penalty?

And so they arrived at this famous old ground with familiar questions around their character, especially after losing to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup, and how they would go about it: go to dominate like they attempted at Bayern Munich, or slip into a more familiar conservative approach?

Their bravery was ultimately rewarded.

Arsenal dug in for long periods, particularly in the first half, but that was simply due to the quality of Liverpool's response to falling behind. They restricted Liverpool to little of note in the second half, aided by a bold substitution as Arteta replaced Bruno Guimarães with the more attack-minded Myles Lewis-Skelly on 62 minutes.

It is fitting that Arsenal went top of the table with a statement win like this. There is now only Premier League ground left in which Arteta has played and never won: Manchester City. -- James Olley

2. Liverpool need to learn from Arsenal's defending

The game was only 20 minutes old when Bruno Guimares celebrated a block inside his own penalty area with the same enthusiasm as if he'd scored a goal. It was an embodiment of Arsenal's unerring commitment to defending, something Liverpool need to learn from if they have ambitions of challenging for major honours in the near future.

articles.headline: Ex-Liverpool, Man City star Milner runs NYC Marathon in just over three hours
articles.description: It's clear James Milner is enjoying his retirement from soccer, as he ran the 2026 NYC Marathon on Sunday with an impressive time. Did we mention he's 40 years old?
articles.body:
James Milner has always been something of a cult hero in soccer, with his work ethic and personable demeanor making him a fan favorite across a 24-year career, especially at the clubs he represented. From Leeds United to Newcastle United, Aston Villa, Manchester City, Liverpool and Brighton, Milner made a career for being the hardest working, indefatigable presence in every team, routinely finishing tops of preseason fitness tests even as he celebrated turning 40 back in January.

He announced his retirement at the end of the 2025-26 season but do you think for one minute that "Milly" has taken it easier now that he's hung up his boots?

Of course he hasn't: On Sunday, he seemingly cruised his way through the 2026 New York City Marathon, completing the course in a remarkable 3:09.04. Not bad, James, not bad at all!

Looking deeper at his split times, it does seem as though Milner took it easy (well, easier) down the stretch, wrapping the first half in 1:31 before going 1:38 for the final 13 miles, but we forgive him for turning it into more of a fun run from there. That said, an average pace of 7:13 per mile is remarkable; it makes us tired just reading it.

What's next, Milner: climbing Mount Everest? Playing in the NFL? We wouldn't bet against him regardless of what he sets his sights on ...

articles.headline: Jalen Brunson joins Harry Styles on stage to cap Styles' MSG residency
articles.description: The superstar singer-songwriter was joined on stage by Brunson, who presented Styles with a commemorative banner for his 30-show Madison Square Garden residency.
articles.headlineJa: ジェイレン・ブランソンがハリー・スタイルズのステージに登場、MSGレジデンシーの締めくくりに
articles.descriptionJa: 超人気シンガーソングライターのステージにブランソンが共演。マディソン・スクエア・ガーデンでの30公演にわたるレジデンシーを記念して、スタイルズに記念バナーを贈呈した。
articles.body:
Harry Styles brings plenty of fame to the stage as-is, but the superstar singer-songwriter's Saturday night performance at Madison Square Garden got an extra boost in star power from a guest plenty familiar with the Garden's spotlight.

Star New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson.

Saturday night marked the 30th show of Styles' Together, Together residency, and he was joined on stage by Brunson, who presented Styles with a commemorative banner for the residency. Brunson, who was received with uproarious "MVP" chants from the home crowd, rocked a hat emblazoned with "TECHNO IS MY BOYFRIEND," which Styles has been known to don himself.

"Can you just make a note, we're almost as tall as each other," Styles joked when the two greeted each other on stage.

"And, yes, I will return your hat," Brunson responded.

It's not the first time during Styles' residency that Brunson has made an appearance. The newly minted NBA champion had already attended two of Styles' previous shows during his stretch of performances at the Garden, getting a shoutout from the singer on Sept. 12.

"We may or may not have the King of New York in the house tonight ... Mr. Jalen Brunson," Styles said during the show. "He's just trying to have a quiet night out -- not a chance. Not in this city. It's like Mickey Mouse going to Disneyland."

Brunson will return to his own Madison Square Garden stage Monday when the Knicks host the Brooklyn Nets.

ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Sunday

November opens with a quartet of NBA games, each of which could prove to be competitive according to betting metrics, as today's point spreads range from just 2.5-6.5 points.

Tighter lines suggest the potential for close games, a welcome environment for fantasy purposes given the greater predictability of playing time and workloads when games are tight and coaching patterns remain steadier.

The action opens with the Orlando Magic hosting the Boston Celtics in a matinee. We won't see Boston's Mitchell Robinson due to planned rest, while Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs are sidelined for the Magic. Learn about a rising two-way Magic guard in the streaming section below.

The Indiana Pacers host the Brooklyn Nets in a contest with a lengthy injury report. The absence of Tyrese Haliburton and Ivica Zubac for the Pacers spells another big role for combo guard Andrew Nembhard. Third-year forward Jarace Walker could help in deeper leagues thanks to his ability to do a little bit of everything.

The LA Clippers' decline includes being underdogs to a Golden State Warriors team that won't have Stephen Curry or Draymond Green due to respective injury-management plans. This all points to a big role for Yaxel Lendeborg, who has proven to be one of the most productive rookies in an already impressive class.

The slate concludes with the Los Angeles Lakers hosting the Toronto Raptors. Kawhi Leonard's knee issues resurfaced recently, putting the offense back in the hands of Scottie Barnes. The Lakers are looking to make up for Friday's embarrassing loss to the Warriors and should field a full roster.

Anthony Black, PG/SG, Magic (rostered in 43.3% of ESPN leagues)
